summaryForCoordinator: CONSENT. This is a record-only gate-row entry and its entire checkable surface is factual, so I resolved every claim against live bytes rather than against the draft's account of itself. All eight full digests recompute — v3 at 13076be2, both Stage A verdicts, COORD, file 08, frozen v1 and v2, and HEAD — and the two short tokens (5d5d778, 3a9442d1) bind to a real commit and to frozen v2's own file08Pin, leaving zero unaccounted hex. The subject measured 4e401843 mode 0444 at the start and again at the end. Live figures all match: 28 of 28 required names, 32 of 32 owners, last gate row DR-G32, DR-G08 and DR-112 lead tokens OPEN, condition 2 at 4 of 32, condition 5 last; no live 26 or 27 appears, the two 26s being frozen v2's historical pin, correctly labelled. I tested the two claims most likely to be quietly wrong. First, 'Claude Stage A returned zero advisories' against a Stage A file that does carry three items: they are severity OBSERVATION with O-numbered ids and explicit notAShouldFixBecause clauses, and the file holds no ADVISORY severity — the house distinction is real, since D-210 named its ADVISORY items explicitly, so the draft's sentence is accurate. Second, 'Same no-cell-edit branch as D-170 through D-210': git log on file 08 shows its last modification is 892236a at D-169, so the span holds end to end. The non-unwrite clause parses to exactly 44 members, 167 through 210 with D-168 present and nothing extra. One thing flagged rather than charged: g08-leftover-join.v3 closes OBL-G08-HARNESS-SPEC by reasoning from v2, the single-reviewer specification, and cites no v3, so once v3 is recorded the closing join trails by one revision — the same shape as CLAUDE-D210-ADV-1. It is an advisory because the draft neither rewrites the join nor re-derives the closure; it reports only what D-188 recorded. Coverage limit: the dispatch forbids reading the other reviewer, so for the Codex adversarial lane I confirmed existence, digest, and mode only, and make no claim about its content.
